text.text_excerpt: This place is great. Everything that hit the table was phenomenal, from the bread n butter (sea salted on top) to the main courses. Our waiter Brian was super nice, very polite, informative, and punctual to the table. Great asset! We came early in the evening on a weekday in April 13, make the booking on Open Table for 7pm. We basically had the entire restaurant to ourselves. We started with the Seafood Gumbo, which was just amazing and super filling. This alone would be enough for someone looking for a lite meal. Fortunately for me, I love to eat and more was to come! Then we had three mini sandwiches, braised pork, lobster mac, and crab cake. Each was delicious. For the main dishes, we ...

we ate here twice. late night: had the caesar salad, and they added salmon for me (bIG piece of salmon, too). better than sex chocolate soufflet - OMIGAD! GET IT! breakfast buffet: eggs were made to order - delish FRESH FRUIT - amazing. strawberries were SO YUM. they even had LYCHEES! Ahh! I was in heaven! yeah, it's expensive. really expensive. but, for this trip, it was worth it. ask for Brian the server. he's great. he even sent up a refrigerator for us!

Located inside the New Orleans Marriott, the 5 Fifty 5 restaurant obviously got its name from its address - 555 Canal Street. Now just FYI, I'm never a big fan of hotel bars. I don't make it a point to go the hotel bar when I'm in town, or even when I travel because anything that's located inside a hotel is normally way overpriced. Unless there's some kind of incentive for me to go, I avoid them. If you read my review for the New Orleans Marriott, then you'll know that during my check in, we were presented with a couple of vouchers.
